All of the workshop's **core materials in one place.** Each analysis **module** pairs **1:1:1:1** across four layers — a slide-deck **lecture**, a long-form **book chapter** (reading), a hands-on **laptop tutorial** (on `ifnb`), and the matching **Talapas HPC script** (the same `ifnb` analysis as a SLURM batch job). Click straight through to any of them. Quick references live on the [Cheat Sheets](Cheat_Sheets.qmd) tab; material *beyond* the workshop — prerequisite appendices, external papers, communities — lives under [Additional Resources](Additional_Resources.qmd).

## Day 0 modules (optional — Tuesday refresher)

A two-hour **computational refresher** the day before the workshop ([Tuesday, June 9 — see Schedule](Schedule.qmd)), for participants who are new to the command line, HPC, or R. Two modules, one hour each — each is a **lecture** plus a long-form **reading**. Not required, but if any of this is rusty, read the chapters before Day 1.

| Module | Topic | Lecture | Reading |
|:--:|---|---|---|
| 1 | Computer System Fundamentals — computers & operating systems, HPC clusters & Talapas, logging in with VS Code, reproducible environments | [Lec D0·1](Lecture_Folder/Lecture_Day0_1_Computer_Systems.html) | [Reading D0·1](Resources_Folder/Chapter_Day0_1_Computer_Systems.html) |
| 2 | R & the Command Line — shell navigation, pipes & redirection, R & RStudio, packages, the tidyverse | [Lec D0·2](Lecture_Folder/Lecture_Day0_2_R_and_CommandLine.html) | [Reading D0·2](Resources_Folder/Chapter_Day0_2_R_and_CommandLine.html) |

## Bonus modules (11–17, self-paced)

Not part of the three-day in-person workshop — work through them on your own time. They fall into **two groups relative to the core pipeline:**

::: callout-important
**Where each bonus module sits relative to the core pipeline**

- **Run *before* the core (raw data → counts): Modules 11–12.** These take raw 10x **FASTQs** through Cell Ranger to the `filtered_feature_bc_matrix/` (RNA) or peak matrix (scATAC) that the core Module 01 picks up. Most participants are *handed* a counts matrix by their sequencing core, so these are optional — but if you ever process your own raw reads, start here. The end-to-end version (raw reads → counts → full analysis) is the [Full Talapas run from raw FASTQs](Resources_Folder/Talapas_FullRun_FromFASTQs.html) roadmap.
- **Run *after* the core (downstream analyses): Modules 13–17.** WGCNA, trajectory & cell–cell communication, scATAC analysis, spatial transcriptomics, and FAIR data sharing all build on a clustered/annotated object (or their own dataset) once you've finished the core sequence.
:::

### Upstream — raw FASTQs → counts (run *before* the core)

Talapas Advanced exercises (need a cluster, a multi-GB reference, and 64+ GB RAM — not a laptop). They are tutorial-only; there is no separate lecture or chapter.

| Module | Topic | Tutorial (view) | Tutorial (download) |

## What's in each layer

- **Lecture** — the slide deck (reveal.js); the in-class summary of the topic.
- **Reading (chapter)** — the long-form prose "textbook" treatment, with worked examples and cross-references to the prerequisite [appendices](Resources_Folder/Reference_Material.html).
- **Tutorial** — a hands-on `.qmd`: **view** the rendered HTML to read along, or **download** the source to open in RStudio (or VS Code on Talapas) and run chunk by chunk (with *Think about it* prompts and collapsible answers). The laptop tutorials run on the laptop-friendly **`ifnb`** dataset.
- **Talapas script** — the *same* tutorial workflow as a streamlined R script you submit to UO's **Talapas** HPC cluster as a SLURM job. Each script is numbered to match its module; the [Talapas pipeline page (Module 10)](Exercise_Folder/Tutorial_10_Talapas_Pipeline.html) collects them.

::: callout-tip
**Recommended order.** Watch the lecture and read the chapter *before* working the matching tutorial: the lecture is the summary, the chapter is the detail, the tutorial is the runnable code, and the Talapas script scales it on the cluster.
:::

## The Talapas HPC track (Friday morning)

The fourth leg of each analysis module is the same `ifnb` analysis as **streamlined R scripts** you submit to Talapas as SLURM jobs — no raw FASTQs and no new dataset (script `01` loads `ifnb` straight from Bioconductor). On Friday morning we work through it as two core modules:

1. **[Module 09 — SLURM Basics](Exercise_Folder/Tutorial_09_SLURM_Basics.html)** — login, modules, interactive sessions, and batch submission, ending with an example batch script (<a href="Exercise_Folder/scripts/run_pipeline.sbatch" download>run_pipeline.sbatch</a>) that runs the whole `01`–`08` series.
2. **[Module 10 — the analysis pipeline](Exercise_Folder/Tutorial_10_Talapas_Pipeline.html)** — the script-by-script table, the generic <a href="Exercise_Folder/scripts/run_rscript.sbatch" download>run_rscript.sbatch</a> wrapper, and the submission commands (e.g. `sbatch run_rscript.sbatch 01_qc_preprocessing.R`).

::: callout-note
**Want the full pipeline from raw FASTQs** (BCL → Cell Ranger → counts → analysis) on a real 10x dataset? That's the optional bonus upstream **Modules 11–12** above and the [Full Talapas run from raw FASTQs](Resources_Folder/Talapas_FullRun_FromFASTQs.html) roadmap.
:::

## Datasets

The laptop tutorials and the Talapas track both run on **`ifnb`**; Module 16 (Spatial) uses **`stxBrain`**, and the other downstream bonus modules (13 WGCNA, 15 scATAC) have their own datasets. Full download URLs, the expected directory layout, and a disk-space budget are on the **[Datasets](Datasets.qmd)** page. A quick data dictionary for the two main objects:

### `ifnb` — Kang *et al.* 2017 (Modules 01–08)

Human peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs), **\~14k cells**, 10x Chromium 3′ v1, loaded via `muscData::Kang18_8vs8()`. Eight lupus donors, each split into a control and an interferon-β–stimulated aliquot — so it has a **real condition** *and* **real biological replicates**, which is what makes integration, pseudobulk DE, and differential abundance meaningful.

| Variable (cell metadata) | What it is |
|---|---|
| `stim` | Condition — `CTRL` or `STIM` (interferon-β, 6 h). The two samples we integrate. |
| `ind` (→ `donor`) | Donor ID — one of **8** lupus patients; the biological replicate for DE / DA. |
| `seurat_annotations` | Author-curated cell type (CD14/CD16 Mono, CD4/CD8 T, B, NK, DC, pDC, Mk…). |
| `nCount_RNA` | Total UMIs (transcripts) detected in the cell. |
| `nFeature_RNA` | Number of genes detected in the cell. |
| `percent.mt` | Percent of reads from mitochondrial genes (added during QC; a stress/quality flag). |

### `stxBrain` — 10x Visium adult mouse brain (Module 16)

A **spatial** dataset: each observation is a **spot** (a ~55 µm patch of tissue containing several cells), not a single cell, and every spot keeps its **x/y position** on the slide. Two sagittal sections — **anterior** and **posterior** — installed via `SeuratData::InstallData("stxBrain")`.

| Variable / slot | What it is |
|---|---|
| `nCount_Spatial` | Total UMIs captured under the spot. |
| `nFeature_Spatial` | Number of genes detected under the spot. |
| `orig.ident` / section | Which tissue section the spot belongs to (anterior vs posterior). |
| `images` slot | The H&E image plus each spot's pixel/tissue coordinates, used for spatial plots. |
